direct: Any service that decodes untrusted Base64 on an affected Java runtime can be crashed or taken over without a login.
downstream: Java is bundled inside third-party applications, appliances and container images, so exposure extends to products you did not build.
Patching depends on each vendor shipping an updated runtime, so some systems will stay exposed after your own servers are fixed.
watch_for: Vendor advisories naming a bundled Java runtime
Unfamiliar Java processes or runtimes on servers

direct: An outsider can run code on the Endpoint Manager Core server without credentials; exploit code is public.
downstream: The Core server can push software and scripts to every managed computer, so a takeover there can become a takeover of the fleet.
Management servers are a common starting point for ransomware deployment.
watch_for: New or unexpected software distribution tasks
Core server reachable from the internet
Unusual SQL errors or new admin accounts on the Core

direct: Attackers are exploiting a flaw that runs code on the Puppet Server.
downstream: The Puppet Server defines configuration for every node it manages, so control of it can change settings or run commands across the estate.
Secrets held in Puppet data, such as service passwords, could be read.

direct: Unfixed flaws let an outsider take control of refrigeration controllers that are reachable from the internet.
downstream: US agencies warn that altered settings can force heating and defrost cycles, causing inventory loss and a fire hazard.
Operators can lose sight of real temperatures, so spoiled goods may not be noticed in time.
watch_for: Setpoint or defrost schedule changes nobody made

direct: Over 6 million stolen credentials were recovered from the criminals' servers and are being shared with notification services.
downstream: Credentials stolen before the takedown may already have been sold and can still be used.
Expect a wave of breach notifications and password resets as victims are told.
watch_for: Notifications from HaveIBeenPwned, Shadowserver or your national CSIRT
Sign-ins from new locations on accounts without multi-factor authentication

direct: Automated agents hunted for exposed AI gateways and app builders and extracted the provider keys inside them.
downstream: Stolen keys were pooled to fund further attacks, so victims see unexpected AI bills.
A key that also grants wider cloud access turns a billing problem into a breach.
watch_for: Unexpected spend or usage on AI provider accounts
AI gateways with default or hardcoded credentials

direct: A widely embedded third-party script was altered, so sites loading it served malicious code to their visitors.
downstream: Every site that loads the script inherits the compromise without being breached itself.
Card or login details entered on affected pages may have been captured, creating notification duties for site owners.
watch_for: Third-party scripts loaded without integrity checks
Unexpected outbound requests from checkout or login pages
